topic.name: Domain and Range of Transformed Reciprocal Functions

question.text: The domain of the function $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{kx-2\sqrt{6}}$ is $\left(-\infty,\sqrt{6}\right)\cup\left(\sqrt{6},\infty\right).$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
A reciprocal function is defined for all values of $x$ except for those that make the denominator zero. So, to find the domain, we must exclude all values that make the denominator zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get

\begin{align*} k x-2\sqrt{6}&=0\\[5pt] k x&=2\sqrt{6}\\[5pt] x&= \dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{k}. \end{align*}

So, the point that must be excluded from the domain is $x = \dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{k}.$

On the other hand, we can see that $x=\sqrt{6}$ is excluded from the domain. Equating this to $\dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{k},$ we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{k}&=\sqrt{6}\\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{k}&=1\\[5pt] k&=2. \end{align*}

question.text: The domain of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{4x+2}{x + 3a}$ is $\left(-\infty,6\right)\cup\left(6,\infty\right).$ What is the value of $a?$
question.explanation:
A reciprocal function is defined for all values of $x$ except for those that make the denominator zero. So, to find the domain, we must exclude all values that make the denominator zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get

\begin{align*} x + 3a &= 0\\[3pt] x & = -3a. \end{align*}

So, the point that must be excluded from the domain is $x = -3a.$

On the other hand, we can see that $x=6$ is excluded from the domain. Equating this to $-3a,$ we get

\begin{align*} -3a & =6\\[3pt] a & =-2. \end{align*}

example.title: Solving for an Unknown Constant in a Transformed Reciprocal Function Given the Domain

question.explanation:
A transformed reciprocal function of the form

\[ f(x) = \dfrac{a}{bx+c} + d \]

has the horizontal asymptote $y=d,$ and therefore, its range is

\[ f(x) \in (-\infty, d)\cup (d,\infty). \]

In our case, $d = -2.$ Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y = -2,$ and the range of the function is

\[ f(x) \in (-\infty, -2) \cup (-2, \infty). \]
